R4B-bear-backcountry-0002.name: 150 m N of Midge Creek
R4B-bear-backcountry-0002.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R4B-bear-backcountry-0002.parkWhat: pull off on Next Creek FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Burn from 2021 (fire N71245), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
S facing slope, 18 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Midge Creek 150 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

flags.t: Route crosses provincial park: Kootenay Lake Park - Midge Creek Site. Hunting only where that park allows it, in open season. Check its bcparks.ca page (synopsis page 9, 99%).
Route crosses private land (ParcelMap BC, updated 2026-10-01): get permission first or go around.
Inside MIDGE CREEK WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT AREA Wildlife Management Area: rules differ by area. Call the regional office before you hunt (synopsis page 9, 99%).

CWD (Chronic Wasting Disease) Management Zone, MU 4-7: every deer, elk and moose taken here must have its head sampled at a CWD freezer before you leave the zone (www.gov.bc.ca/CWDdropoff). Brain and spinal column (vertebrae, not the tail) may not leave the zone: leave them at the kill site or a landfill in it (synopsis pages 15, 36, 37, 99%).

Region 4: it is unlawful to feed or bait deer, elk, moose and other hoofed game, or turkeys, anywhere in the Kootenay Region (synopsis page 37, 99%). Snowmobiles may not be used for hunting in Region 4 from 1 April to 30 November (page 37, 99%).
Wolf: no closed season in MU 4-7 below 1,100 m (synopsis page 39 footnote, 90%: the Trench line is not mapped and "below 1,100 m" is my reading for both groups). VERIFY with the regional office.

seasonRows.notes: bag 2; private land only, with landowner permission

plan: Drive: from Boswell, about 18 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Hwy 3A, Lower Wynndel Rd, Hwy 3, Blazed Creek FSR.
Park: 49.33004, -116.79251, pull off on Next Creek FSR (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 5.5 km N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 740 m, about 183 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 420 m SW of the spot at 603 m (49.37324, -116.82534). Water: Midge Creek 20 m N (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).

Legal: MU (Management Unit) 4-7, Region 4. CWD zone: deer, elk and moose heads go to a CWD freezer; brain and spine stay in the zone. No baiting in Region 4. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-01, closures 2026-10-16.

R4B-grouse-atv-0001.name: By Akokli Creek
R4B-grouse-atv-0001.pressureWhy: Busier: within 1 km of a paved road (estimate).
R4B-grouse-atv-0001.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (Hwy 3A); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: Road: Akokli Creek FSR, 7.1 km stretch.
100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
9 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
12 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.

flags.t: Route crosses private land (ParcelMap BC, updated 2026-10-01): get permission first or go around.
Private land right here: no shooting within 100 m (109 yd) of an occupied house or farm building (synopsis page 10, 99%).
Hwy 3A right here: no hunting or shooting on or across the road allowance of a numbered highway or 2 lane public road, 15 m (16 yd) each side of the centre line (synopsis page 10, 99%).

CWD (Chronic Wasting Disease) Management Zone, MU 4-6: every deer, elk and moose taken here must have its head sampled at a CWD freezer before you leave the zone (www.gov.bc.ca/CWDdropoff). Brain and spinal column (vertebrae, not the tail) may not leave the zone: leave them at the kill site or a landfill in it (synopsis pages 15, 36, 37, 99%).

Region 4: it is unlawful to feed or bait deer, elk, moose and other hoofed game, or turkeys, anywhere in the Kootenay Region (synopsis page 37, 99%). Snowmobiles may not be used for hunting in Region 4 from 1 April to 30 November (page 37, 99%).
Wolf: no closed season in MU 4-6 below 1,100 m (synopsis page 39 footnote, 90%: the Trench line is not mapped and "below 1,100 m" is my reading for both groups). VERIFY with the regional office.

seasonRows.notes: No row in the Region 4 table (pages 39 and 40), so no general open season (page 5: open seasons are only those in the synopsis). Pages 36 to 41 print no LEH list.

plan: Drive: from Boswell, about 4 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Hwy 3A.
Park: 49.42616, -116.75326, where the truck road ends (Hwy 3A); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: the Akokli Creek FSR stretch, 7.1 km one way. About 141 min one way at 3 km/h.
Hunt: grouse, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Walk slowly in the first and last 2 hours of light. Watch where cutblocks and creeks meet the road (Tip).
Use: .22 rimfire for a sitting grouse inside 25 m (27 yd), or a shotgun with lead 6 or 7.5 (Tip).
